children: Technology stocks are heading into Thanksgiving with their
The
State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF
is down 22.4% since Sept. 30, from $195.75 to $151.85, including a 15.4% drop in November alone.
Nvidia Corp.
sits at the center. The stock is down 33.9% this month, its worst since 2008, and is headed for a seventh straight weekly loss, matching its longest streak on record, set in July 2008.
California Attorney General
Rob Bonta
said “red flags have been raised” in a Bloomberg Television interview about Nvidia and its former chief executive,
Jensen Huang
. “We’re aware and we’re looking,” Bonta said.

In Washington, a new Commerce Department rule on remote access to advanced chips, expected to take effect Nov. 19 according to law firm Morgan Lewis, requires a U.S. license for foundries shipping certain chips designed by China-headquartered companies.
The
Invesco QQQ Trust
traded at $621.70 on Friday, down 8.6% on the week.
The selloff reached the hardware names reporting next.
Dell Technologies Inc.
fell 10.1% on Friday and
Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.
dropped 8.4%.
Among other large companies,
Analog Devices Inc.
carries a 7.86% implied move before Tuesday’s open, and
Deere & Co.
carries 6.84% before Wednesday’s open.
The widest expected swings, however, sit in software, servers and retail.
These are the 10 largest expected movers of the week, among U.S. stocks with at least $10 billion in market cap, according to
data.
An implied move is the percentage swing in either direction that options traders expect right after earnings.
Which Stocks Could Swing The Most This Week?
10. Best Buy: 9.33% Implied Move
The consumer electronics retailer reports Tuesday, Nov. 24, before the open, for its fiscal third quarter.
The Street expects earnings of $1.49 per share on $9.89 billion in revenue.

Analysts have been raising targets into the report: BofA Securities lifted its target to $83 but kept an Underperform rating on Friday, UBS moved to $103 with a Neutral rating on Nov. 17, and Telsey Advisory Group raised its target to $110 with an Outperform rating on Nov. 16.
Holiday guidance, comparable sales and tariff-related pricing will drive the reaction.
Best Buy Co. Inc.
is up 48.72% year to date.
9. HP: 9.78% Implied Move
The personal computer and printer maker reports Tuesday, Nov. 24, after the close, for its fiscal fourth quarter.
Analysts model earnings of 74 cents per share on $15.36 billion in revenue, against 93 cents per share and $14.64 billion a year earlier.
Morgan Stanley raised its target to $21 on Nov. 16 and kept an Underweight rating.
Memory costs, PC demand and fiscal 2027 guidance are the items to watch.
HP Inc.
is up 27.20% year to date.
8. Dollar Tree: 10.09% Implied Move
The discount retailer reports Tuesday, Nov. 24, before the open, for its third quarter.
Consensus calls for earnings of 88 cents per share on $5.05 billion in revenue, compared with $1.21 per share and $4.75 billion a year earlier.
Stifel initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $160 target on Nov. 17, and UBS raised its target to $165 on Nov. 16. Loop Capital had downgraded the stock to Hold on Nov. 5.
Comparable sales, margins and the holiday outlook are the main variables.
Dollar Tree Inc.
is up 13.29% year to date.
7. Workday: 10.25% Implied Move
The human resources software company reports Tuesday, Nov. 24, after the close, for its fiscal third quarter.
Analysts expect earnings of $2.45 per share on $2.69 billion in revenue.
Workday announced on Nov. 18 its intent to acquire Honeydew, according to
Subscription revenue growth, margins and the impact of artificial intelligence on software demand are the key questions.
Workday Inc.
is down 16.73% year to date.
6. Autodesk: 10.47% Implied Move
The design software maker reports Tuesday, Nov. 24, after the close, for its fiscal third quarter.
The Street expects earnings of $2.91 per share on $2.13 billion in revenue, up from $2.67 per share and $1.85 billion a year earlier.
Loop Capital upgraded the stock to Buy with a $310 target on Nov. 13.
Billings, margins and full-year guidance are the items to watch.
Autodesk Inc.
is down 16.30% year to date.
5. Dick’s Sporting Goods: 12.24% Implied Move
The sporting goods retailer reports Tuesday, Nov. 24, before the open, for its third quarter.
Consensus calls for earnings of $1.38 per share on $5.06 billion in revenue, compared with $2.78 per share and $4.17 billion a year earlier.
Wells Fargo raised its target to $195 with an Overweight rating on Nov. 13, while Cantor Fitzgerald initiated at Neutral with a $146 target on Nov. 10.
Comparable sales, margins and holiday guidance will set the tone.
Dick’s Sporting Goods Inc.
is down 32.25% year to date.
4. Hewlett Packard Enterprise: 12.43% Implied Move
The enterprise hardware company reports Monday, Nov. 23, after the close, for its fiscal fourth quarter.
Analysts expect earnings of $1.26 per share on $14.42 billion in revenue, against 62 cents per share and $9.68 billion a year earlier.
UBS lowered its target to $52 on Friday and kept a Neutral rating. Citigroup cut its target to $80 and Morgan Stanley to $64 on Nov. 16, both keeping positive ratings.
Artificial-intelligence server demand, margins and fiscal 2027 guidance are the items to watch.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise
is up 73.53% year to date.
3. Nutanix: 13.66% Implied Move
The hybrid cloud software company reports Tuesday, Nov. 24, after the close, for its fiscal first quarter.
Analysts expect earnings of 54 cents per share on $0.76 billion in revenue.
Rosenblatt reiterated a Buy rating with a $75 target on Nov. 17, and Guggenheim initiated coverage with a Buy and a $100 target on Oct. 26.
Subscription renewals, margins and full-year guidance will drive the reaction.
Nutanix Inc.
is up 6.66% year to date.
2. Zoom Communications: 13.92% Implied Move
The video and collaboration software company reports Monday, Nov. 23, after the close, for its fiscal third quarter.
Analysts expect earnings of $1.39 per share on $1.28 billion in revenue, compared with $1.52 per share and $1.23 billion a year earlier, according to
StoneX lifted its target to $130 with a Buy rating on Thursday, and Citigroup raised its target to $131 on Nov. 17. BTIG lowered its target to $115 on Nov. 18 and kept a Buy rating.
Enterprise customer growth, margins and full-year guidance will drive the reaction.
Zoom Communications Inc.
is down 4.67% year to date.
1. Dell Technologies: 15.70% Implied Move
The computer and server maker reports Tuesday, Nov. 24, after the close, for its fiscal third quarter.
Analysts expect earnings of $6.55 per share on $49.48 billion in revenue, compared with $2.59 per share and $27.01 billion a year earlier, according to Benzinga Pro.
Citigroup lowered its target to $550 and kept a Buy rating on Nov. 16, while Morgan Stanley cut its target to $403 with an Equal-Weight rating the same day.
Artificial-intelligence server orders, margins and fiscal 2027 guidance are the items to watch.
Dell
is up 123.18% year to date.

title: Earnings Volatility Watch: Dell And 9 Other Stocks Are Priced For Swings Of 9% Or More
